title: Project: A Complete Application
summary: Designing and building a whole application from the course's parts - a budget tracker with a domain library, commands parsed from input, services behind interfaces, JSON persistence with versions, reports with LINQ, error handling at the edges, tests, and where to go next with C#.

cards.q: Why is the report a pure function of the ledger and the month?
cards.a:
It can be tested with any ledger built in memory, with no side effects to set up or clean up

A pure function's result depends only on its arguments, so a test just builds a ledger and checks the report. No files or clock are involved.

cards.q: Why store a version number in the saved file?
cards.a:
So a later version of the app can recognise and convert files written by older versions

When the format changes, the version number tells the loader which layout it is reading, so old files keep working.

cards.q: In this design, where should the rule "an amount of 0 is not allowed" be checked?
cards.a:
In the domain, in Ledger.Add

Rules live in the domain so every way of adding a transaction obeys them; the command handler at the edge turns the error into a message.
